name: Chatha Foods Ltd
tagline: Small-cap B2B frozen / processed-food supplier to QSR chains (Domino's/Jubilant, Subway, Burger King) - a proxy for ~20% QSR-industry growth, with a completed 3x capacity expansion (Allana JV + new Mohali plant) and an unusually transparent, honest promoter - but pass-1 primary-document review found the operating-leverage inflection has NOT shown up a full year after capacity completion (FY26 revenue +5.4%, margin +19bps) despite an aggressive FY27-29 guidance ramp, and a prior FY25 growth guide was already missed
business_overview: Mohali-based frozen and ready-to-eat / ready-to-cook meat processor operating a B2B model for QSRs, cafes and institutional clients (chicken appetisers, patties, sausages, sliced meat, toppings). Has exited the low-margin hotel and B2C segments historically and re-focused on B2B, where 5-6 month customer audit/qualification cycles act as an entry barrier. FY26: completed a ~3x capacity expansion - a new Rs 42-44cr, 14 KTPA Mohali facility (flatbreads/tortillas/parathas/gravies/frozen-to-fried, commissioned Mar-2025, production from Jul-2025, breakeven at ~45% utilisation, peak revenue potential Rs 175-200cr) plus the Allana CF Foods JV (Rs 40cr capex, Chatha holds 70% equity, 6 KTPA RTC + 4.5 KTPA RTE, Allana contractually purchases 100% of the JV's output for export - a genuine committed-offtake structure for that specific line, though the standalone new veg capacity has no disclosed anchor B2B clients). The Allana JV reached operational readiness with commercial scale-up guided for Jul-2026. In late 2025 the company launched a D2C/B2C brand 'Unifayre' (RTE/RTC, targeting UAE/Gulf + domestic) despite prior guidance of no B2C plans. Management guidance (Feb-2026 investor call) targets revenue of Rs 325cr+ (FY27), Rs 450cr+ (FY28), Rs 550cr+ (FY29) with EBITDA margin reaching 12-13% (FY26-27) and PAT margin 9-10% by FY29 (implying PAT ~5-6x the FY24 base) - a very steep ramp against FY26's actual delivery of Rs 166cr revenue (+5.4% YoY) and 7.4% EBITDA margin (+19bps YoY). (Source: forum discovery, first_seen 2026-09-07; deep-dive pass 1, 2026-09-18.)
fundamentals_table: ~9.5% / ~8% (Sep-26) - declining from ~19% (FY23) / ~25.8% peak (FY19); erratic 10-yr history (MoneyWorks4Me: ROCE swung -15.8% to 25.8%)
FY26 actual +5.4% YoY (Rs 166 Cr) - well below the 5yr/3yr averages (~22%/~12%) and far below the guided FY27 ramp to Rs 325 Cr+ (~96% YoY)
FY26 actual 7.4% (+19bps YoY) - management guides 12-13% for FY26-27; a prior FY25 revenue-growth guide of 20% was also missed

Trade receivables doubled YoY (Rs 11 Cr -> Rs 22 Cr); cash conversion cycle worsened to ~42 days (Mar-25) from ~24 days - a watch item, though one FY26 snapshot shows a shorter 13-day figure (source discrepancy, unresolved)
fundamentals_narrative: Pass-1 primary-document review confirms the capacity is real and physically complete (14 KTPA new Mohali plant + Allana JV, ~16,000 MTPA total) but the operating-leverage inflection management and the forum expected has not materialised one full year on: FY26 revenue grew just 5.4% to Rs 166cr and EBITDA margin expanded only 19bps to 7.4%, both far short of a prior FY25 guide of 20% revenue growth and the FY26-27 margin guide of 12-13%. Management's Feb-2026 guidance (Rs 325cr FY27, Rs 450cr FY28, Rs 550cr FY29, PAT 5-6x by FY29) requires the ramp to roughly double revenue in FY27 alone off a base that just grew 5.4% - a large guidance-credibility gap. The one genuinely new positive: the Allana JV has real committed offtake (Allana buys 100% of that line's output for export), which de-risks that specific piece of new capacity even though the standalone new veg plant still has no disclosed anchor client. ROCE has fallen from ~19% (FY23) to ~9.5% as capacity was added ahead of volume, and an independent quality read (MoneyWorks4Me) flags a decade of erratic ROCE/ROE and negative operating-cash-flow-to-debt. The Unifayre B2C pivot cuts against the prior B2B-only discipline and is showing up as doubled receivables and rising marketing spend, adding working-capital and execution risk on top of an unproven core ramp.
technical_read: Not pulled - the call rests on whether the operating leverage shows up in FY27 numbers, not chart position.
sentiment_summary: 34-post thread, cautiously positive and engaged. Strong appreciation for Chatha's transparency - it publishes transcripts of closed-door PMS/fund-manager calls, which Marathondreams (trusted, elevated) singled out. Debate centres on the B2C pivot: some (Marathondreams) see higher long-run growth/margin if executed in a calibrated way; others (sandesh, AnkitAgrawal) find it strange to launch B2C while the Allana JV and veg plant are still ramping, and worry it signals a thin B2B client pipeline for the new capacity. Latest post (Sep-26): Marathondreams on the FY26 annual report, 'founder promoter comes across as honest hard working... ready for the grind'.
community_signal: Marathondreams (trusted, elevated tier - not core) has been invested for ~1 year and repeatedly states 'continues to add as story improves' - a sustained accumulate, not a one-shot high-conviction call. Broad community tenor is constructive-but-watchful on execution and the B2C pivot.

verdict_headline: Pass-1 deep dive: capacity is real and the Allana JV has genuine committed offtake, but a full year after the 3x expansion completed, the operating-leverage inflection has NOT shown up (FY26 +5.4% revenue, +19bps margin) and management's own FY27-29 guidance ramp follows a missed FY25 guide - thesis_fit stays 'neither', conviction moves down to Low-Medium pending FY27 quarters that actually demonstrate the ramp.
verdict_reasoning: four_box: tailwind yes (QSR industry ~20% CAGR, frozen-food penetration, QSR processing outsourcing - real and multi-year), tam yes (16,000 MTPA capacity vs tiny current load = big operating-leverage runway; only ~Rs 254 Cr market cap), moat weak (5-6 month qualification cycles are a real barrier, but customer concentration and stretching receivables limit pricing power), valuation downgraded to no (P/E ~37.9 against FY26's actual 5.4% growth/7.4% margin and a guidance-credibility miss is not supported by demonstrated execution) -> score 2.5

Score 2.5 falls in the 2.0-2.5 band, which defaults to thesis_fit 'neither' unless a written exception applies (valuation=yes, un-ignorable growth, or the large-cap named-inflection carve-out) - none apply here since growth was only 5.4% and valuation itself moved to 'no' -> 'neither' stands without needing an override flag

value_chain.position: B2B processing layer - manufactures the frozen meat and RTE/RTC inputs that QSR chains and institutional foodservice buy rather than make in-house; sits between poultry/raw-protein suppliers and the branded QSR outlets. Logistics for contract volumes is handled by the QSR client.
value_chain.bottleneck_node: filling the newly-tripled capacity with anchor customers - the standalone new veg plant has no disclosed committed clients
value_chain.note: Chatha itself just added ~3x processing capacity ahead of demonstrated demand - a company-specific late-cycle-glut risk until utilisation and new-client wins catch up; the QSR-outsourcing tailwind for the industry as a whole remains intact.

growth_trajectory.last_quarters_note: Revenue CAGR has decelerated from ~22% (5yr) to ~12% (3yr) to ~5.4% (FY26/TTM); H1 FY26 revenue ~Rs 84cr vs H2 FY25 ~Rs 83cr shows little visible acceleration despite the 3x capacity coming online during the period.

management_quality.capital_allocation: Rs 42-44cr new plant + Rs 40cr Allana JV (70% Chatha equity) funded via modest debt (~Rs 26cr) plus an equity raise; capacity built well ahead of demonstrated demand, with returns not yet proven
management_quality.capability_ladder_note: Explicit move from commodity B2B processing to a branded 'Unifayre' D2C/export line, plus Allana-JV-enabled Middle East export access

track_record.note: FY24 (+14.5% rev/12% ROCE) and FY25 (+17.2% rev/10% ROCE) missed on ROCE (<15%); FY26 (+5.7% rev) missed on revenue growth (<10%) and ROCE (~9.5%). ROCE fell from ~19% (FY23) to ~9.5% as the 3x capacity expansion landed ahead of volume - no year clears both filters yet. Independent source (MoneyWorks4Me) corroborates a longer erratic history: ROCE swung from 25.8% (FY19) to -15.8% (FY21) to 11.9% (FY25).

quality_metrics.note: Rs ~26cr total debt (Mar-26) against FY26 EBITDA of ~Rs 12.3cr (7.4% of Rs 166cr) gives net_debt_to_ebitda ~2.1x. FCF conversion stayed deeply negative through the capex phase (independent source confirms CFO turned negative, -Rs1.1cr FY25); capex_efficiency is 'unclear' because the claimed '4x asset turn' on the new automated lines is management's own unproven target, not yet demonstrated by utilisation data.

shareholding_pattern.note: Promoter holding stable at ~55.6-55.8% with 0% pledge across the checked quarters - no promoter-exit signal. FII (2.86%) + DII (13.35%) institutional interest is modest but present.

working_capital.note: Cash conversion cycle lengthened from ~24 days to ~42 days (per MoneyWorks4Me, FY25) and trade receivables doubled YoY (Rs 11cr -> Rs 22cr) - a genuine cash-drag warning that coincides with the Unifayre B2C launch, though revenue growth itself has been modest (+5.4% FY26), so this isn't yet a growth-funded-by-working-capital story so much as a margin/collections one.
